subject: CAIQ + ephemeral debug logs: handling and evidence timeline
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@plenumhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_ops@plenumhealth.com
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ artifacts + ephemeral debug log handling (customer request)

Hi Rafael —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Two items we need to close our security review for the integration: a) the CAIQ artifacts you referenced (answers + evidence files) and b) confirmation on handling of ephemeral debug logs.

Specifically, Plenum's Security team requires that debug traces which may include minimally processed PII (error payloads, truncated user identifiers) be deleted within 14 days of creation. Our SOC 2 auditor will ask for:
- a short description of the retention workflow for tenant-scoped debug traces
- sample proof-of-delete artifacts we can present (hashes, deletion job runIDs, S3 lifecycle records)
- the CAIQ evidence pack you maintain for ephemeral log retention controls

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a 14-day TTL for Plenum's tenant with an attestation/certificate we can attach to our audit? If there are compensating controls required, we need these spelled out.

Target timeline: we'd like the evidence pack in 3 business days if possible. Let me know the next steps and any intake form you need us to sign.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lopez
Director, Security & Compliance
Plenum Health

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@plenumhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ artifacts + ephemeral debug log handling (customer request)

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: we can support a targeted tenant-level retention adjustment, but there are operational and compliance trade-offs to document. I’m looping in Kim (policy & product) and Priyom (forensics/runbook) to produce a short evidence pack and a proposed delivery schedule.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Internal: Kim & Priyom to confirm exact artifacts we can produce and any required addendum (e.g., a TTL addendum to the contract).
- External: Rafael will provide a one-page attestation (template) and an evidence bundle with sample proof-of-delete runs.

I’ll aim to get a formal response and attachments by end of day tomorrow (Mon 06/25).

Thanks —
Rafael
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2028 17:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ artifacts + ephemeral debug log handling (customer request)

Rafael / team —

Context and what we can deliver:

1) Default behavior:
- Tenant-scoped "ephemeral debug traces" are retained by default for 30 days in the debug bucket. Retention is driven by a lifecycle policy + periodic background purge job.
- For SOC 2 we retain immutable audit records (runIDs, deletion job receipts, signed deletion manifests) for 90 days to support evidence needs.

2) Customer-specific TTL (what we can support):
- We can implement a tenant-specific TTL shortening to 14 days, but to preserve our incident forensics posture we require the customer to accept a "forensics-limited" addendum: Redwood will capture metadata (deletion manifests, jobIDs) for 90 days, but full payloads will be retained no longer than 14 days for that tenant.
- Compensating controls we recommend if you opt for 14-day payload retention:
  * Enable tenant-level request tracing (trace IDs preserved outside payloads for 90 days)
  * Enforce redaction rules at ingestion for user-identifying fields (we can supply a redaction ruleset)
  * Optional: retain shortened partial payloads (headers + non-PII fields) for 30 days to assist debugging without PII exposure.

3) Evidence artifacts we can produce in the requested timeline:
- Retention matrix (redwood_ttl_matrix_202806.pdf) — maps artifact types to retention windows and proof-of-delete artefact types.
- Sample proof-of-delete (proof_of_delete_sample-20280625.txt) — contains a deletion manifest example, S3 lifecycle event snippet, and job runID.
- Tenant purge runbook (tenant-purge-runbook-Plenum.zip) — sanitized runbook showing the automated purge process and the manual reconciliation steps for deletions.

4) Implementation notes / lead time:
- Tenant TTL change is a config flag + automated purge commit. We can schedule the change in a maintenance window; low-risk, ETA 3 business days for standard path. If the customer requires on-call forensic hold or additional logging, add 5 business days for policy & config review.

I’ll attach the artifacts and a proposed customer-facing attestation text. Priyom — can you add the sample deletion manifest and confirm the exact manifest fields we include for auditor review?

—Kim
Principal Product Manager, Data Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@plenumhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ artifacts + ephemeral debug log handling (customer request) — evidence bundle and proposed schedule

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the patience — attached is a tailored evidence bundle for Plenum. Summary below and next steps.

What we included (attachments):
- redwood_ttl_matrix_202806.pdf: retention windows for debug traces, KV cache artifacts, and audit manifests
- proof_of_delete_sample-20280625.txt: sanitized example deletion manifest + S3 lifecycle event snippet + purge job runID
- tenant-purge-runbook-Plenum.zip: sanitized runbook showing automated purge and manual reconciliation steps

Our recommended approach for Plenum's 14-day requirement:
1) TTL change: set tenant debug-trace TTL to 14 days (payloads).
2) Compensating controls (required): preserve deletion manifests and runIDs for 90 days (auditor-facing), enforce ingestion redaction rules (we will supply a ruleset), and enable trace-ID-only retention for 90 days.
3) Delivery timeline: if Plenum agrees to the addendum language below, we can schedule the TTL change and deliver the attestation within 3 business days. If you require KMS key rotation proof or additional audit logs, add 2 business days.

Proposed attestation (excerpt):
"Redwood Inference confirms that for tenant 'Plenum Health' the ephemeral debug trace payloads will be purged no later than 14 days after creation. Deletion manifests (including runIDs and signed deletion receipts) will be retained for 90 days and made available to the customer for audit purposes upon request. Plenum Health agrees that shortened payload retention may limit Redwood's ability to perform long-term incident reconstruction and accepts the compensating controls described in the attached addendum."

If that language looks good I can:
- publish a short TTL addendum (DocuSign link) for signature
- schedule the tenant config change in our maintenance window and run a proof-of-delete job once complete

Attachments and link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Plenum-CAIQ-evidence-20280625 (contains the three files listed). DocuSign addendum: https://docusign.com/placeholder/Plenum-ttl-addendum

Next step from you: confirm you accept the compensating controls or tell us if you need a different balance between payload retention and forensics capability. Once confirmed, we’ll push the config change and provide the proof-of-delete output.

Best,
Rafael

Attachments: redwood_ttl_matrix_202806.pdf, proof_of_delete_sample-20280625.txt, tenant-purge-runbook-Plenum.zip

From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@plenumhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_ops@plenumhealth.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ artifacts + ephemeral debug log handling (customer request)

Rafael / team —

Thanks — that looks tidy and addresses most of our auditor's checklist. Quick question before we sign the addendum: does the retention change include any change to how KMS keys are rotated or to key access logs? Our compliance team wants confirmation that key rotation events and key usage logs remain available for 90 days even if payloads are purged at 14 days.

If that's covered, we can sign the addendum and ask you to proceed with the change.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah

We will include a KMS audit excerpt in the evidence bundle (rotation events + usage logs) before you sign.

—Neha
